cards.cue: Describe a person who has had an important influence on your life.
points: how long you have known them
what they have done for you
cards.end: and explain why this person has had such an influence on you.
part3: What kinds of people are role models for young people today?
Do you think celebrities have a positive or negative influence on children?
How has the influence of parents on children changed compared with the past?
Are teachers as respected now as they used to be?
cards.sample:
The person I'd like to talk about is my secondary school chemistry teacher, Mrs Aydın. I first met her when I was about thirteen, so I've known her for around ten years now, and we still keep in touch occasionally.

To be honest, I wasn't a particularly good student at the time. I found science quite intimidating, and I'd more or less convinced myself that I just wasn't a 'science person'. What made her different was that she never made anyone feel stupid for asking questions. She used to stay after class to go through problems with me step by step, and she'd always relate abstract ideas to everyday things, like why bread rises or why ice floats.

The turning point came when she encouraged me to enter a regional science competition. I was terrified, but she helped me prepare for weeks, and although I didn't win, I got an honourable mention, which completely changed how I saw myself.

I think the reason she had such an influence on me is that she taught me that ability isn't fixed: if you're patient and you're willing to make mistakes, you can get much better at almost anything. That attitude has stayed with me ever since, and to be honest, it's one of the reasons I'm preparing for this exam so seriously now.

cards.cue: Describe a place you would like to visit in the future.
cards.end: and explain why you would like to visit this place.
part3: Why do people enjoy travelling to other countries?
What are the negative effects of tourism on local communities?
Do you think virtual reality could replace real travel?
How has travel changed in the last fifty years?
cards.sample:
One place I've wanted to visit for a long time is Kyoto, the old capital of Japan. I first became interested in it a few years ago when I watched a documentary about traditional Japanese architecture, and since then I've read quite a lot about it.

What appeals to me most is the contrast between old and new. Japan is famous for its technology, but Kyoto has kept more than a thousand temples and shrines, as well as traditional wooden houses and beautiful gardens. If I went there, I'd love to spend a few days just walking around the historic districts early in the morning, before the crowds arrive. I'd also like to stay in a ryokan, which is a traditional inn where you sleep on mats on the floor, and try the local food, especially the vegetarian dishes served in the temples.

I think the main reason I want to go is that it seems like a place where people have managed to preserve their history without rejecting modern life, and I find that really inspiring. It would also be a completely different experience from anywhere I've been before, so I imagine I'd learn a great deal.

cards.cue: Describe a piece of technology you find useful.
cards.end: and explain why you find it useful.
part3: Has technology made people's lives easier or more stressful?
Should children be taught to use technology from an early age?
What jobs might disappear because of technology?
Do older people find it difficult to adapt to new technology?
cards.sample:
I'd like to talk about a fairly simple piece of technology that has made a surprisingly big difference to my life: a pair of noise-cancelling headphones. I bought them about two years ago, mainly because I was commuting by bus for over an hour each day and found it impossible to concentrate.

I use them almost every day. On the bus I listen to podcasts, mostly in English, which has actually helped my listening skills quite a lot. When I'm studying at home, I often put them on without any music at all, just to block out the noise from the street and my neighbours. And occasionally, on long flights, they make it possible to sleep.

I find them useful for a couple of reasons. First, they've made my commute productive rather than wasted time, because I can learn something while I travel. Second, and probably more importantly, they help me focus. I live in a busy area, and before I had them I used to get distracted constantly. If I'm honest, I didn't expect a pair of headphones to have such an impact, but I'd now find it hard to manage without them.
